findings.issue: Issue_WhenAnotherTrackedEntityViolatesAnUnrelatedConstraint_PropagatesTheOriginalException_NotMisreadAsARace never reaches IsSequenceRaceException, so the medium finding it claims to cover has no coverage at all. The test uses the private two-argument IssueAsync helper, which calls IOfficialNumberService.IssueAsync(kind, now) -> ClockCheckService.CheckAsync, and CheckAsync unconditionally calls db.SaveChangesAsync (ClockCheckService.cs:73) on the SAME WakeelDb before IssueCoreAsync ever runs. That first save flushes the invalid Setting (settings.value is NOT NULL, migration line 101) and throws DbUpdateException there — before any OfficialNumber row is tracked and before the numbering try/catch exists. The assertion therefore holds for any DbUpdateException from the clock check and would still pass if IsSequenceRaceException were reverted to the over-broad `SqliteErrorCode == 19` form the finding was about. The two assertions inside are also weak: Assert.ThrowsAsync<DbUpdateException> is an exact-type match in xunit, so Assert.IsNotType<OfficialNumberConcurrencyException>(ex) can never fail, and ContainsSqliteException is trivially true for any EF constraint failure.
findings.fix: Route the test through the explicit-verdict helper so the numbering SaveChanges is the first save on the context: replace `await Assert.ThrowsAsync<DbUpdateException>(() => IssueAsync(InOutDirection.Out, date));` with `await Assert.ThrowsAsync<DbUpdateException>(() => IssueAsync(InOutDirection.Out, date, ClockVerdict.Ok));` (the three-argument private helper already opens the transaction and calls the ClockVerdict overload, which skips ClockCheckService entirely). Then make the assertion non-vacuous by proving the failure was seen by the numbering catch and rejected: assert `ex.Entries` contains the offending Setting and does NOT contain an OfficialNumber (`Assert.Contains(ex.Entries, e => e.Entity is Setting); Assert.DoesNotContain(ex.Entries, e => e.Entity is OfficialNumber);`) and that no number was committed (`Assert.Empty(_session.Db.OfficialNumbers.AsNoTracking())` after the rolled-back transaction). Drop the unreachable Assert.IsNotType line.

findings.issue: IsSequenceRaceException narrows only the SqliteException branch to this row; the first branch, `exception is DbUpdateConcurrencyException`, still matches regardless of which entity lost the concurrency check. Because IssueCoreAsync's SaveChangesAsync flushes every other change the caller tracked on the same context, a concurrency conflict on an unrelated tracked entity that carries its own concurrency token is misclassified as this (kind, year) row's race: the service silently swallows the caller's real conflict, spins EffectiveMaxConcurrencyAttempts pointless attempts, and finally reports it as OfficialNumberConcurrencyException — exactly the misattribution the fixed branch was narrowed to prevent. No duplicate number can be issued (nothing is committed), so the impact is diagnostic, not correctness of numbering.
findings.fix: Require this row in Entries for both branches, e.g. rewrite the expression body as: `=> exception.Entries.Any(e => ReferenceEquals(e.Entity, row)) && (exception is DbUpdateConcurrencyException || (exception.InnerException is SqliteException { SqliteErrorCode: SqliteConstraintErrorCode } sqlite && sqlite.SqliteExtendedErrorCode is SqlitePrimaryKeyConstraint or SqliteUniqueConstraint));` and update the XML doc's second-case-only wording accordingly.

findings.issue: The recovery path added for the medium finding — `if (db.Entry(row).State == EntityState.Added) { db.Entry(row).State = EntityState.Detached; }` after ReloadAsync — is executed by no test. In Issue_WhenAnotherContextInsertedTheVeryFirstRowFirst_IsRetried_AndTheNumbersDiffer the reload finds the winner's committed row, so the entry flips to Unchanged and the detach branch is skipped; Issue_WhenRetriesAreExhausted_... runs with maxConcurrencyAttemptsForTests: 1, so it throws before any reload happens and never exercises a second loop iteration either. A regression that removed the detach (reintroducing EF's untranslated identity-conflict InvalidOperationException on the next Add) would keep all 173 tests green.
findings.fix: Add one test that makes the first attempt fail while the row is still absent from the database and then succeed on the second: construct the service with maxConcurrencyAttemptsForTests: 2, track an Added OfficialNumber for (Out, 2026) on a second DbSession whose (kind, year) row is NOT committed by any other context, force the insert to fail once (e.g. pre-insert and then delete the winner's row on the other connection, or use the same tracked-Added setup and roll the winner's transaction back before the loser saves), and assert the call returns sequence 1 rather than throwing InvalidOperationException about a tracked instance with the same key. Assert the entry for the discarded instance ends Detached.

SPEC ITEM 1 (INSERT race) — implemented and genuinely tested. IsSequenceRaceException now demands SqliteErrorCode 19 plus extended code 1555 (PRIMARY KEY) or 2067 (UNIQUE) plus `exception.Entries.Any(e => ReferenceEquals(e.Entity, row))`; the catch reloads, detaches a still-Added row, and retries within the bounded loop. Issue_WhenAnotherContextInsertedTheVeryFirstRowFirst_IsRetried_AndTheNumbersDiffer is a real two-DbSession test over the same file: the loser's tracked Added instance really hits a PRIMARY KEY violation and the retry yields sequence 2 with a distinct number; it fails if the catch is removed. Uniqueness under concurrency holds in both directions: last_seq is an IsConcurrencyToken, so the UPDATE race re-reads; the INSERT race re-queries and takes the winner's row; the whole read-modify-write runs inside the caller's transaction (EnsureInTransaction is still enforced on both overloads and is still covered, including the "nothing was written" assertions), and EF takes a savepoint for SaveChanges under a user transaction, so a failed attempt leaves nothing half-applied. No path can hand out the same (kind, year, seq) twice, and no path can commit a number without the caller's transaction.

IErrorMapper remains registered and used elsewhere (ErrorMapper.cs, ErrorMapperTests, ServiceRegistrationTests) so nothing is orphaned, and DI still resolves OfficialNumberService: the new 3-argument test seam is internal, so only the public 2-argument constructor is visible to the container.
